_doc: What each case's main.rs measures relative to the main.ts every TS runtime runs. same = same algorithm and allocations (rust uses integers where TS has number; tr narrows when it can prove it). suppressed = black_box / dyn Fn deliberately block devirtualization or inlining, so the rust row is a floor for calls, not for the hardware. different = rust does less or other work. hardev/autorun/bench_latest.sh refuses a rust row that is not listed here.

ackermann.lead: tr inlines the self-call one level, which rustc does not: more instructions retired, fewer cycles

fib40.caveat: rust-fast emits the same fib machine code as rust (2.89G instructions in both) but places the recursion loop where it takes 840M cycles against 700M; built with -C llvm-args=-align-all-nofallthru-blocks=6 it reads 701M. Its row here is a code-placement reading, not a ceiling; against rust tr reads 0.92 work-only (mini 2026-10-03)

generic-pair-1m.why: the pair never escapes, so it is a local struct; rustc is free to reduce the loop

objlit-optional-field-1m.why: the record never escapes, so it is a local struct with an Option; rustc is free to keep it in registers

split-only-100k.why: collects a Vec<&str> every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count
split-only-100k.note: both split operands are literals, so the whole call can be folded at compile time; split-only-argv-100k takes them from argv

split-only-1m.why: collects a Vec<&str> every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count
split-only-1m.note: both split operands are literals, so the whole call can be folded at compile time; split-only-argv-100k takes them from argv

split-only-argv-100k.why: collects a Vec<&str> every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count

map-str-100k.why: std HashMap with SipHash-1-3; tr hashes keys with FNV-1a

dict-count-optional-read-1m.why: std HashMap with SipHash-1-3, the record an Option field; tr hashes keys with FNV-1a

array-copy-1m.why: black_box(src[j]) per element blocks the memcpy the loop is

array-map-1m.why: Box<dyn Fn> + black_box keep the callback an indirect call

closure-counter.why: Box<dyn Fn> + black_box + inline(never) forbid devirtualization

closure-counter-renamed.why: closure-counter with the captured binding not spelled like the top-level one; Box<dyn Fn> + black_box + inline(never) forbid devirtualization

collatz.why: u64 n & 1 and n >>= 1 where main.ts needs f64 % 2 and / 2 (int32 ops would overflow)

rpn-eval-100k.why: lazy split iterator and a fixed stack array; JS split materializes an array

csv-trim-100k.why: lazy split iterator; JS split materializes an array

csv-rebuild-100k.why: lazy split iterator; JS split materializes an array

throw-catch-100k.why: panic + catch_unwind stands in for throw / catch

regex-dfa-anchored-100k.why: hand-written matcher for ^\w+; no regex engine, no compiled automaton

regex-dfa-dotall-100k.why: hand-written matcher for a.+c (s flag); no regex engine, no compiled automaton

regex-dfa-iflag-100k.why: hand-written eq_ignore_ascii_case scan for hello; no regex engine

regex-dfa-mflag-100k.why: hand-written matcher for ^line (m flag); no regex engine

regex-dfa-safeclass-100k.why: hand-written byte-class scan for [A-Za-z0-9]+; no regex engine

regex-dfa-uflag-100k.why: hand-written utf-8 decode + \p{L} range-table scan; no regex engine

regex-dfa-uflag-cprange-100k.why: hand-written byte-class scan for [A-Za-z]+ (u flag); no regex engine

regex-dfa-wbound-100k.why: hand-written matcher for \bword\b; no regex engine

regex-wireback-minlit-100k.why: hand-written byte search for x; no match array, index or input props

regex-wireback-minlit-10m.why: hand-written byte search for x; no match array, index or input props

array-any-indexed-100k.why: Vec<String> has no per-element type tag; main.ts reads an any[] and dispatches on the tag

array-any-double-sum-1m.why: Vec<f64> has no per-element type tag; main.ts reads an any[] and dispatches on both operands' tags

array-any-str-to-num-1m.why: Vec<String> has no per-element type tag, and str::parse::<f64> accepts a narrower grammar than ToNumber (no whitespace trim, no 0x / 0b / 0o prefix); same strings, one conversion per iteration

i64-to-str-100k.lead: each formatted Str is popped from tr's 32-slot small-string pool and pushed back on drop; rustc's String is a libmalloc malloc and free per number

i64-to-str-10m.lead: each formatted Str is popped from tr's 32-slot small-string pool and pushed back on drop; rustc's String is a libmalloc malloc and free per number

multibyte-concat-5m.why: Vec<u16> holds the UTF-16 code units a JS string has, so .length is len(); the piece is a constant [u16; 4] as the literal is in main.ts and main.c, appended in place with doubling capacity from 16 units
multibyte-concat-5m.lead: the mechanism of main.c: the Vec reallocs through libsystem_malloc at each doubling, tr grows acc through its own arena size classes; rust 289M instructions / 43M cycles, C 269M / 40M, tr 208M / 31M (mini 2026-10-03)

multibyte-concat-flat-5m.why: Vec<u16> holds the UTF-16 code units a JS string has; the piece is a constant [u16; 4], appended in place with doubling capacity from 16 units, then the last unit is read
multibyte-concat-flat-5m.lead: the mechanism of main.c: the Vec reallocs through libsystem_malloc at each doubling, tr grows acc through its own arena size classes; rust 293M instructions / 43M cycles, C 269M / 39M, tr 208M / 31M (mini 2026-10-03)

class-method-100k.why: black_box keeps both per-iteration Box allocations, which LLVM would elide

class-method-10m.why: black_box keeps both per-iteration Box allocations, which LLVM would elide

str-concat-ascii-100k.why: black_box keeps the per-iteration String, which LLVM would elide and fold the loop

str-concat-ascii-escape-100k.why: the concat is loop-invariant: tr and bun build it once before the loop and store the same string every iteration; main.rs allocates a fresh string every iteration (str-concat-ascii-vary-10m is the case where every runtime must build it)
str-concat-ascii-escape-100k.note: at n=100k bun's work is mostly JIT warm-up (about 690 instructions per iteration against about 24 in steady state), so this ratio favours tr; str-concat-ascii-escape-10m reads the steady state

str-concat-ascii-escape-10m.why: the concat is loop-invariant: tr and bun build it once before the loop and store the same string every iteration; main.rs allocates a fresh string every iteration (str-concat-ascii-vary-10m is the case where every runtime must build it)

str-concat-ascii-vary-10m.why: each result is a fresh String from concat, moved into an 8-slot ring that drops the String it replaces, and read back by index

json-stringify-100k.why: serializer is fixed to the struct's keys and value kinds; JSON.stringify discovers both at run time

str-replace-100k.why: hand-coded forward scan for a(b+)c stands in for a regex engine

str-replace-argv-100k.why: hand-coded forward scan for a(b+)c stands in for a regex engine

async-fn-call-100k.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

async-suspend-5m.why: step is a spawned task whose state machine queues its own resumption for the await null, so each call is two fifo round trips as in the spec; the yield allocates no promise, since the one the spec creates for null is never observable

promise-all-1m.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-await-100k.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-chain-1m.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-then-100k.caveat: the receiver is Promise.resolve of a number, a fresh fulfilled cell no code has seen: tr's module body runs the then reaction and the await's continuation in place, in the spec's job order, and makes no derived promise (the fused await p.then(f) lane, at its fresh-fulfilled receiver). Sibling with a pending receiver held in a binding: promise-then-pending-100k

promise-then-pending-100k.why: later is a spawned task whose state machine queues its own resumption for the await null; the then reaction waits in the still-pending promise's list and settles the derived promise the loop awaits, three fifo round trips per iteration as the spec orders
promise-then-pending-100k.caveat: tr makes no derived promise here (the await is its only reader); Rust allocates and settles one

generator-yield-100m.note: rustc inlines the iterator and reduces each pass to a closed form, so the rust row keeps no work after startup at any size

split-materialize-1m.why: collects a Vec<&str> borrowing the line, the shape of tr's split block of views over the parent string: one array allocation per line, no copy per field; the rebuilt String is appended in place from empty
split-materialize-1m.lead: the rebuilt cell grows through tr's in-process string pool where rustc's String goes through libmalloc every line
split-materialize-1m.caveat: tr does not materialise here: parts is only read as parts[k] in order, so the index loop is rewritten into the split iterator and no array exists; siblings: split-materialize-escape-1m, split-materialize-store-1m

split-materialize-escape-1m.why: collects a Vec<&str> borrowing the line and moves it into a binding that outlives the loop, dropping the previous line's Vec; the rebuilt String is appended in place from empty
split-materialize-escape-1m.lead: rustc's Vec and String go through libmalloc every line, 43% of its samples; tr's rebuilt cell grows through its string free-list pool: 9% fewer instructions retired (4.14G against 4.56G)

split-materialize-store-1m.why: the split of main.c: counts the separators, allocates the Vec<&str> once at its final size and fills it with views into the line, then stores it into a 1024-slot Vec<Vec<&str>>, dropping the Vec it replaces; every slot is read after the loop; the rebuilt String grows by doubling from 16, as main.c

throw-unwind-depth8-1m.why: Result<i64, Box<Fail>> propagation stands in for throw / catch; the finally body runs inline in every frame, no unwinder

str-build-1mb.why: String appended in place, grown by doubling from empty; no capacity hint

tokenizer-parser-eval-10k.why: tokens stored inline in a Vec (the Rust best form; tr also stores them inline), Box per AST node; int32 wrapping arithmetic in evaluate

regex-capture-exec-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures are written as their own String and the digits parsed from the captured one, but only the length of the key is read, so rustc is free to remove that allocation

regex-replace-callback-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures and the replacer's result are their own String, the output String is appended in place with no capacity hint
